## Design

### 2026-10-12 – Devlog 01: first layout

**2h**

Devlog 01: first layout

started the rotating pcb vise for CAD week. i want something that can hold a board while soldering, turn over to reach the other side, and take different grips for different boards

made the first layout in FreeCAD with a freestanding base, two uprights, a rotating frame and sliding jaw bodies on steel rods. the starting range is for boards 30-160 mm wide. the important sizes are editable, including the board dimensions, rod diameter and rotation height

checked the ESC before deciding how to grip it. the right edge has pads and connector tabs where a straight jaw would go, so the first adapter uses its four mounting holes instead. the spacing is 109 x 105 mm. generic edge grips still need designing

the saved assembly has 27 valid solids. checked rotation every 15 degrees, with no intersections between the moving assembly and the base at those positions. board widths of 30, 116 and 160 mm recompute correctly, and the STEP export imports with all 27 solids. this uses an empty board outline, so it doesn't prove clearance around all the real components

modelled a small fit sample to print in PLA with four rod-hole sizes and four M6 nut-pocket sizes. it will help choose the clearances before printing all the parts. the printer is a P1S, and i have PLA, PETG-CF and TPU for AMS available

next are the jaw lock, pivot fasteners, adapter attachment and base joints. the model is still a layout, with no physical fit or load tests yet

### 2026-10-14 – Devlog 02: clamps, pivots and base

**4h**

Devlog 02: clamps, pivots and base

finished the main connections that were missing from the first layout. each jaw now has a slit and an M4 screw to clamp it around the front guide rod. added the captured nuts and washer clearances too. the jaw positions are adjusted by hand and locked with an Allen key

the ESC adapters now bolt onto the jaws with M3 screws. made a second pair of TPU inserts with grooves for ordinary board edges. both options use the same attachment holes, so they can be swapped without changing the jaw bodies. the ESC still uses its four mounting holes because its edge is crowded

worked out the pivot hardware instead of leaving plain cylinders as placeholders. the M6 bolt heads sit in hex pockets in the carriers. the outer knobs hold M6 nuts, with steel washers outside the uprights and TPU friction rings inside. the actual holding force still needs testing

added bolted lap joints to the base bars and recesses where they fit into the feet. the upright screws pass through the bars too. made screw-on ballast lids and slip-on TPU shoes. the first collision check found the outer lid-screw tips touching the shoes, so added blind relief pockets with material left underneath

checked the assembly with the fasteners included. no overlaps remain in the default assembly, and the frame clears the fixed parts at 24 sampled rotation angles. both insert configurations recompute without printed-part collisions at board widths of 30, 116 and 160 mm. the STEP export contains all 109 assembly solids

exported 28 prototype STLs, including the two alternative edge grips. all meshes are closed and fit the P1S envelope. adjusted the print orientations and enlarged the carrier faces to support the pivot discs. added a small M3/M4/M5 nut-pocket sample alongside the earlier rod and M6 sample

updated the hardware quantities, assembly instructions and README. nothing has been printed or load-tested yet. next are the fit samples, one jaw-clamp test, pivot friction and base stability, then the final shopping list
